chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him), my brother, and ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Sa‘īd, from ‘Abd al-Malik al-Qummī, from Ismā‘īl ibn Jābir, from ‘Abd al-Ḥamīd – the servant of Ismā‘īl ibn Ja‘far, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

The prayer is completed (in full form, without shortening) in four locations: in the Sacred Mosque (Masjid al-Ḥarām), and the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and the Mosque of Kūfah, and the Sanctuary of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him).

key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الرَّسُولِ: The Mosque of the Messenger (in Medina)

ai.seo_question: Where are prayers performed in full form (not shortened) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the unique spiritual status of Imam al-Husayn’s shrine by equating it with the three primary centers of Islamic authority: the Ka‘bah, the Prophet’s Mosque, and the Mosque of Kūfah. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes a specific exception to the general rule of *qasr* (shortening prayers during travel), emphasizing the sanctity of these four locations as places where the full four-rak‘ah prayer is obligatory even for travelers. This ruling underscores the theological elevation of the Ahl al-Bayt’s shrines to the level of major mosques in Islamic law.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. My father, my brother, and ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain all narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Ḥusain ibn Sa’īd, (from Muḥammad ibn Sinān), from ‘Abdil Malik Al-Qummi, from Ismā’īl ibn Jābir, from ‘Abdil Ḥamīd – the servant of Ismā’īl ibn Ja’far, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
You can establish (the obligatory) prayers in full form in four locations: in Masjid Al-Ḥarām, in the Mosque of the Messenger (s.a.a.w.), in the Mosque of Kūfah, and in the Ḥaram of Ḥusain (a.s.).”
